title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
why_read: A candid, well-argued post pushing back on agent hype by describing a real production experience where a simpler pipeline beat a supposedly autonomous agent.
analysis: The author describes building an LLM-based agent with planning and reasoning loops, only to discover in production that it always executed the same three steps regardless of its 'autonomy,' and that a plain linear pipeline was faster, cheaper, and easier to debug. This is a useful, grounded counterpoint to marketing narratives around agentic AI, focused on observability, cost, and reliability tradeoffs that matter in real deployments. It doesn't introduce new techniques but offers a practical lesson many engineers building LLM systems will recognize. Reasonably interesting as a caution against over-engineering AI systems when a fixed workflow suffices.
